subject: top 5 markets for 2026
headline: Where the cap rate plus appreciation math still works.
body: These are the five markets where, as of mid-2026, you can still buy quality rentals with reasonable cap rates AND credible appreciation upside. Not the cheapest. Not the highest cap. The best combined math.

Nashville: 5.5-6.5% caps in B-class submarkets, 3-4% rent growth, strong job creation. Davidson County tax is rising but still manageable. The flip side: prices have run hard, so deals require patience.
Indianapolis: 7-8% caps in B-class areas, 2-3% rent growth, light property tax (~1%), no income tax for landlords structured right. Boring market, in the best way.
Memphis: 8-9% caps possible, but you're working harder on the operations side. Vacancy can hit 10-12%. PM quality varies wildly. Best for investors with local presence or a great team.
Birmingham: 7.5-8.5% caps, slow appreciation (1-2%), very low property tax (0.4%), and a quietly improving downtown. The 10-year math is better than the year-one numbers suggest.

Tampa: 5-6% caps but the appreciation tailwind is real. Insurance is the wildcard — model 12-15% annual premium growth and stress-test the deal. Skip the coastal flood zones unless you really know what you're doing.
Run any of these through TrueCap and you'll see why the numbers work. Or don't.
